children.title: Financial results
children.summary: This page serves as a title slide for the financial results presentation covering the first fiscal quarter of 2026 (FQ1 2026). The visual design features a large, abstract graphic on the right side depicting a grid-like structure with vibrant purple and blue lighting, likely representing microchip technology or data processing. The text is presented in white against a dark purple gradient background.

children.title: Safe harbor statement
children.summary: This page contains a 'Safe harbor statement' from Micron, warning that the presentation includes forward-looking statements regarding market demand, technology impacts (such as AI), and financial projections. It advises readers to refer to SEC filings like Form 10-K and 10-Q for risk factors and notes that the company is not obligated to update these statements except as required by law. The text also defines non-GAAP financial measures used in the presentation.

children.title: Sanjay Mehrotra
children.summary: This page is a presentation slide featuring Sanjay Mehrotra, identified as the Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer. The layout includes his name and title on the left side and a professional headshot of him on the right. The document is marked 'Micron Confidential' and dated December 17, 2025.

children.title: Overview (1 of 3)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Overview (1 of 3)', outlines Micron's strong financial performance for fiscal Q1 and the full year of fiscal 2026. It highlights record-breaking revenue across total company, DRAM, NAND, HBM, and data center segments. The text also details completed supply agreements for calendar 2026 HBM and forecasts a significant growth in the High Bandwidth Memory Total Addressable Market (TAM), projecting it to reach approximately $100 billion by 2028.

children.title: Overview (2 of 3)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Overview (2 of 3)', outlines Micron's strategic position in the AI market. It highlights progress on the HBM roadmap and emphasizes that memory has become a critical asset for AI cognitive functions across data centers and edge devices. The company anticipates substantial financial growth in revenue, gross margin, and EPS for the second quarter and fiscal year 2026.

children.title: Overview (3 of 3)
children.summary: This page is the third part of an overview, discussing market conditions and production strategy. It notes that strong industry demand and supply constraints are expected to persist beyond 2026. The company is making progress on multiyear contracts with customers and is focused on maximizing production output by ramping up technology nodes and investing in new cleanroom space.

children.title: Technology and operations (1 of 2)
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Technology and operations (1 of 2)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Technology and operations (1 of 2)', outlines Micron's technology leadership in the semiconductor industry. It highlights that Micron has led for four consecutive DRAM nodes and three NAND nodes with improving yield ramps. The text details the ramp-up of the 1-gamma DRAM node as a primary driver for bit growth in calendar 2026 and mentions ongoing development for future 1-delta and 1-epsilon nodes.

children.title: Technology and operations (2 of 2)
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Technology and operations (2 of 2)
children.summary: This page, titled 'Technology and operations (2 of 2)', outlines Micron's progress in NAND technology. It details the ramping of the G9 node for data center and client SSDs, noting a record high QLC NAND mix. The text projects that G9 will drive bit growth in calendar 2026 and become the largest NAND node later in fiscal 2026. Additionally, it highlights that Calendar 2025 was a record year for Micron regarding quality measures.

children.title: Data center server demand
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Data center server demand
children.summary: This slide outlines the increasing demand for data center servers driven by advancements in artificial general intelligence and a multiyear buildout. It highlights that server unit growth is expected to be in the high-teens percentage range for calendar 2025, surpassing previous outlooks, with strength continuing into 2026. The content concludes by noting Micron's portfolio of solutions, including HBM and SSDs, designed to meet these evolving memory and storage requirements.

children.title: Data center HBM and LP DRAM
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Data center HBM and LP DRAM
children.summary: This page outlines Micron's strategy and progress regarding Data Center HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) and LP DRAM. It details the timeline for HBM4 ramp-up in 2026, highlighting its speed and manufacturing capabilities. Additionally, it discusses Micron's leadership in Low Power (LP) DRAM, specifically mentioning the sampling of a 192GB LP SOCAMM2 product that offers significant capacity increases.

children.title: Data center NAND
children.summary: This page outlines the performance and product updates for Micron's data center NAND portfolio. It highlights that revenue exceeded one billion dollars in fiscal Q1 and details the introduction of the world's first PCIe Gen6 SSD using G9 NAND technology. The text also notes robust demand for mainstream storage products in early 2026 and mentions capacity storage solutions entering qualification at hyperscale customers.

children.title: PC
children.summary: This page outlines the PC market outlook, attributing demand to the Windows 10 end-of-life and the rise of AI PCs. It forecasts high-single-digit growth in unit sales for calendar 2025 and notes potential supply constraints in 2026. Additionally, it highlights that Micron has completed OEM qualifications for its 16Gb 1-gamma-based DDR5 memory and G9-based PCIe Gen4 QLC SSDs.

children.title: Mobile
children.summary: This page outlines Micron's mobile strategy and market outlook, projecting low-single-digit growth in smartphone unit volumes for calendar 2025. It highlights that AI is driving memory content growth, with flagship smartphones containing 12GB of DRAM reaching a 59% shipment mix in Q3. The slide details Micron's innovation progress, including the sampling of breakthrough 1-gamma 16Gb LPDDR6 products and volume shipments of 1-gamma LP5x 16Gb products to OEMs.

children.title: Automotive and embedded
children.summary: This page outlines Micron's strategy and market position in the automotive and embedded sectors. It highlights that L2+ and L3 autonomous vehicle adoption is driving demand for higher memory content, with Micron leveraging its product portfolio to secure billions in design wins. The text also notes strong demand in industrial applications like factory automation and robotics, supported by investments in supply from the Manassas, Virginia fab.

children.title: Market outlook (1 of 2)
children.summary: This page, titled 'Market outlook (1 of 2)', outlines the current and projected state of the memory and storage industry. It attributes a sharp increase in demand to AI data center build-outs and predicts that supply will remain insufficient for the foreseeable future. The text highlights specific challenges regarding HBM demand versus DDR5 trade ratios, the need for additional cleanroom space, and expects tight market conditions across DRAM and NAND through at least 2026.

children.title: Market outlook (2 of 2)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Market outlook (2 of 2)', outlines updated industry expectations for DRAM and NAND bit demand growth in calendar 2025, projecting low 20% growth for DRAM and high-teens for NAND. It further forecasts that industry shipment growth in 2026 will be constrained by supply, with both sectors expected to increase around 20% from 2025 levels. The text notes that Micron aims to grow its own shipments by approximately 20% in 2026 but expresses disappointment regarding its inability to meet customer demand across all market segments.

children.title: Supply efforts (1 of 2)
children.summary: This page outlines Micron's supply efforts, detailing a planned increase in fiscal 2026 capital expenditure to $20 billion to support HBM and 1-gamma supply. It highlights accelerated timelines for the first Idaho fab (expected mid-2027) and construction of a second Idaho fab starting in 2026. Additionally, it mentions progress on securing permits for a New York site with a planned groundbreaking in early 2026.

children.title: Supply efforts (2 of 2)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Supply efforts (2 of 2)', outlines the company's manufacturing and technology investment strategies across various global locations. It details investments in Japan supported by METI, DRAM technology transitions coordinated with the Boise R&D team, and cleanroom expansion at the Hiroshima fab. Additionally, it covers progress on an HBM packaging facility in Singapore targeting 2027 supply, pilot production at an assembly and test facility in India ramping in 2026, and a commitment to disciplined capex planning.

children.title: Mark Murphy
children.summary: This section presents the financial revenue for Fiscal Quarter 1 of 2026 (FQ1-26), reporting a total of $13.6 billion. It highlights significant growth, noting that revenue increased by 21% quarter-over-quarter (Q/Q) and by 57% year-over-year (Y/Y).

children.title: DRAM FQ1-26
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Performance by technology/DRAM FQ1-26
children.summary: The section titled 'DRAM FQ1-26' outlines the financial performance of DRAM technology for the first quarter of 2026. It reports a revenue of $10.8 billion, which accounts for 79% of total revenue. The text highlights significant growth metrics, including a 69% year-over-year increase and a 20% quarter-over-quarter increase in revenue. Additionally, it notes that bit shipments were up slightly Q/Q and ASPs increased by approximately 20% Q/Q.

children.title: NAND FQ1-26
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Performance by technology/NAND FQ1-26
children.summary: The section titled 'NAND FQ1-26' outlines the financial performance of Micron's NAND technology for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026. It reports revenue of $2.7 billion, which accounts for 20% of total revenue. The section details a 22% year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increase in revenue, bit shipments that grew in the mid-to-high single-digit percentage range Q/Q, and Average Selling Prices (ASPs) that increased in the mid-teens percentage range Q/Q.

children.title: Quarterly business unit financial results
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Quarterly business unit financial results
children.summary: This page presents a table titled 'Quarterly business unit financial results' for Micron, detailing financial performance across four business units: Cloud Memory (CMBU), Core Data (CDBU), Mobile and Client (MCBU), and Automotive and Embedded (AEBU). The data covers three fiscal quarters (FQ1-26, FQ4-25, and FQ1-25) and lists Revenue in millions, along with Gross margin and Operating margin percentages for each unit.

children.title: Financial performance by business unit (1 of 2)
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Financial performance by business unit (1 of 2)
children.summary: This slide details the financial performance of two specific business units: Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU) and Core Data Center Business Unit (CDBU). It highlights record revenues for both units, noting that CMBU generated $5.3 billion (39% of total revenue) and CDBU generated $2.4 billion (17% of total revenue). The text also outlines significant sequential growth in revenue and gross margins for both units, driven by increased bit shipments and higher pricing.

children.title: Financial performance by business unit (2 of 2)
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Financial performance by business unit (2 of 2)
children.summary: This slide details the financial performance of two specific business units: Mobile Client Business Unit (MCBU) and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU). It highlights record revenues for both units, noting that MCBU revenue was $4.3 billion (31% of total) and AEBU revenue was $1.7 billion (13% of total). The text further breaks down sequential growth drivers, such as higher pricing and bit shipments, along with gross margin percentages for each unit.

children.title: FQ1-26 Non-GAAP operating results
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/FQ1-26 Non-GAAP operating results
children.summary: This page presents the Non-GAAP operating results for Micron's fiscal quarter 1 (FQ1-26). Key financial metrics include revenue of $13.64 billion, a gross margin of 56.8%, and net income of $5.48 billion. The document also lists diluted earnings per share at $4.78 and cash from operations (GAAP) at $8.41 billion.

children.title: Cash flow and capital allocation
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Cash flow and capital allocation
children.summary: This page details Micron's cash flow and capital allocation strategy from fiscal year 2023 to the first quarter of 2026. It highlights a total return of $2.7 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends, alongside specific financial metrics for FQ1-26 such as $8.4 billion in operating cash flow and $4.5 billion in net Capex. The document also outlines liquidity figures and upcoming dividend payments.

children.title: AI use at Micron
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/AI use at Micron
children.summary: This slide, titled 'AI use at Micron', outlines the company's adoption of Generative AI and agentic AI across various departments. It highlights that over 80% of the professional workforce uses GenAI, with significant productivity gains in R&D, manufacturing, and coding teams. The page concludes by stating expectations for AI to strengthen Micron's competitiveness in the coming years.

children.title: Outlook
children.summary: This document page, titled 'Outlook' and dated December 17, 2025, presents Micron's financial guidance. It details expectations for gross margin expansion in Q2 due to favorable pricing and costs, projected operating expenses of $1.38 billion for fiscal Q2, and a tax rate of around 15.5%. Additionally, it outlines capital spending plans of approximately $20 billion for fiscal 2026 to address supply/demand conditions and forecasts strengthening free cash flow.

children.title: FQ2-26 guidance Non-GAAP
children.summary: This page presents the Non-GAAP financial guidance for Micron's Fiscal Quarter 2 of 2026 (FQ2-26). It details projected metrics including Revenue ($18.70 billion), Gross margin (68.0%), Operating expenses ($1.38 billion), and Diluted earnings per share ($8.42), each accompanied by a specific variance range.

children.title: Appendix
children.summary: December 17, 2025 30 Appendix

children.title: Financial summary
children.summary: This page presents a Non-GAAP Financial Summary table for Micron, detailing key financial metrics in millions of dollars. The data covers three fiscal periods: FQ1-26, FQ4-25, and FQ1-25, including Revenue, Gross margin, Operating income, Net income, Diluted earnings per share, Cash provided by operating activities, and total cash holdings.

children.title: Non-GAAP financial data and guidance
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Appendix/Non-GAAP financial data and guidance
children.summary: This page presents Non-GAAP financial data and guidance for Micron, specifically detailing performance metrics for Fiscal Quarter 1 of 2026 (FQ1-26) and providing guidance for Fiscal Quarter 2 of 2026 (FQ2-26). The content is organized into tables showing revenue breakdowns by product type (DRAM and NAND), sales volume changes, ASP changes, and key financial figures such as gross margin, operating expenses, and diluted earnings per share. It also includes estimates for diluted shares, income tax benefits, cash from operations, and capital expenditures.

children.title: Revenue by technology
children.summary: The section titled 'Revenue by technology' presents two tables detailing Micron's financial performance across different memory technologies. The first table breaks down revenue in millions for DRAM, NAND, and Other (primarily NOR) categories for fiscal quarters FQ1-26, FQ4-25, and FQ1-25, alongside their respective percentage of total revenue. The second table provides the same revenue figures but includes columns for Quarter-over-Quarter (Q/Q) and Year-over-Year (Y/Y) percentage changes.

children.title: Revenue by business unit
children.path: Micron investor report 530bd7ed.pdf/Root/Appendix/Revenue by business unit
children.summary: The page displays a financial table titled 'Revenue by business unit' from Micron, dated December 17, 2025. The table details revenue in millions for four business units—Cloud Memory (CMBU), Core Data (CDBU), Mobile and Client (MCBU), and Automotive and Embedded (AEBU)—comparing figures across fiscal quarters FQ1-26 and FQ4-25, alongside year-over-year data for FQ1-25.

children.title: Non-GAAP reconciliations
children.summary: December 17, 2025 36 Non-GAAP reconciliations

children.title: Consolidated results
children.summary: This section presents a series of tables detailing the Non-GAAP reconciliations for Micron's consolidated financial results. The tables reconcile GAAP figures to Non-GAAP measures across multiple periods (FQ1-26, FQ4-25, and FQ1-25), covering gross margin, operating expenses, cost of goods sold, research and development, selling/general/administrative expenses, net income, income tax, adjusted EBITDA, diluted earnings per share, and adjusted free cash flow.

children.title: FQ2-26 guidance
children.summary: The section titled 'FQ2-26 guidance' presents a Non-GAAP reconciliation table for Micron's financial outlook. It details the GAAP Outlook, specific adjustments (labeled A, B, and C), and the resulting Non-GAAP Outlook for key metrics including Revenue ($18.70 billion ± $400 million), Gross margin (68.0% ± 1.0%), Operating expenses ($1.38 billion ± $20 million), and Diluted earnings per share ($8.42 ± $0.20). A second table breaks down the Non-GAAP Adjustments in millions, attributing them to stock-based compensation across cost of goods sold, research and development, and selling/general/administrative expenses, as well as tax effects.
